Rechecks after reconnect, foreground return and periodically while open so temporary/public addresses can refresh. Context also tells Mrkdwn which workspace message links can navigate in-place.

entries.plain: A setup checklist that ticks itself off as you create a channel, invite someone, turn on notifications and join a huddle.
entries.summary: Shows setup steps that complete from actual workspace/account behavior.
details: Tracks creating a channel, inviting someone, enabling notifications and participating in a huddle, with account/workspace-local dismissal memory.
The checklist can disappear after completion or explicit dismissal. N04's screen wiring makes its huddle action use the preference-aware join operation.

entries.plain: A banner asking to turn on browser notifications, which waits two weeks before asking again if you pick Not now.
entries.summary: Requests browser notification permission from an intentional visible gesture.
details: Appears after sign-in rather than asking from an unrelated first click. Not now defers the banner for two weeks on this device.
An explicit browser denial remains quiet until site permission changes, and the native desktop notification adapter does not need this banner.

entries.plain: Reads out new messages to screen reader users without moving focus, grouping bursts so they are not flooded.
entries.summary: Politely announces new visible messages without flooding a screen reader.
details: A single arrival includes a bounded excerpt; a burst groups count and up to a few sender names after a quiet period.
Announcements do not steal focus, and navigation clears old-conversation waiting messages so they are not announced in the new destination.

entries.plain: The button at the top of a conversation that starts a huddle, joins one in progress or shows you are in it.
entries.summary: Header control that starts a huddle, joins the running one, or says you are in it.
details: Names the action by the room's state (Start a huddle, Join the huddle (n), In huddle) and joins through the same preference-aware path as other entry points.

entries.plain: The call bar showing who is in the huddle, who is speaking, each person's volume and anyone you cannot connect to.
entries.summary: Shows call presence, speaking rings and the header join/start control.
details: HuddleFace resolves participants and speaking state, while the compact bar hosts controls and a way to restore hidden video.

The list of who is there (Everyone in the huddle) gives each of the others a PersonVolume row. Someone muted for you is said to be, ahead of talking, with a crossed speaker on their face. The bar hands everyone's volume to HuddleAudio.
HuddleButton starts or joins through the shared call-preference store and provides meaningful error state. N04 makes this header path agree with Getting started about mute initialization.
Once a peer's connection has a diagnosed trouble, the bar says Can't connect to them and offers Why? See the call log.

entries.plain: The mute, camera, screen share and leave buttons, with menus to switch microphone, speaker or camera.
entries.summary: Provides shared microphone, camera, screen-share and leave actions.
details: Used by both the compact bar and fullscreen stage so the call actions stay available in either layout.
Stable accessible names plus aria-pressed describe toggles; captureFailure distinguishes a cancelled picker from a permission/device problem. A lost microphone exposes retry.

Beside Mute and Camera, a small arrow opens a menu of microphones and speakers, or cameras, with the chosen one ticked (menuitemradio) and a link to Voice & video settings. The menus are left out of the full-screen overlay, because menus open on the page beneath a fullscreen element.

entries.plain: Plays everyone's voice in a call through your chosen speaker at the volume you set, even with the video hidden.
entries.summary: Keeps each remote microphone playing independently of video layout.
details: Peer audio elements attach microphone streams even when the call has no camera or the video stage is hidden.
Playback refusal produces a recovery action; one user gesture retries blocked peers while already audible streams are left intact. This avoids duplicate audio from video elements.
Each peer's audio element plays through the speaker chosen in Voice & video settings.

Each person plays as loud as you chose. Up to 100% the element's own volume does it, so the usual path is untouched. Past 100% their stream goes through a Web Audio gain into a stream the same element plays, so the chosen speaker still applies. A second, muted element holds their stream meanwhile, since Chromium gives an audio graph silence from a call's stream that no element plays (measured: 0 without it).
A boost's graph that will not start without a gesture is reported like a refused play, so Turn on sound starts it.

entries.plain: One person's volume control in a call, with a mute just for you and a slider up to 200 percent.
entries.summary: One person's volume in a call: mute for you, and a slider from silent to 200%.
details: A toggle button (aria-pressed) mutes the person for you alone, and a range input in steps of 5 sets their volume, with a tick at 100% from a datalist and the percent beside it, or Off.
Moving the slider unmutes them, since it means wanting to hear them. Used in the bar's list of who is there and inside a stage tile.

entries.plain: The video area of a call, which lays out cameras and screen shares as large as the window allows.
entries.summary: Arranges cameras and shares into docked, gallery, presenting or spotlight views.
details: stageItems prioritizes screen shares then participants; bestFit tries column counts to find the largest 16:9 tiles for the actual container dimensions.
Video surfaces stay muted because HuddleAudio owns voices. Local self-video and remote camera/share streams display without opening a second media capture.
Resize observation updates layout, and accessible tiles/actions expose focus, fullscreen and share controls. Lazy loading keeps the stage out of initial conversation downloads until needed.

Another person's tile, in the gallery or the main view, has a volume button beside Pin. Its PersonVolume opens inside the tile rather than as a popover, because popovers portal to the page beneath a fullscreen element. A tile says when its person is muted for you.

entries.plain: Lets you hear and see how your microphone sounds before a huddle, without sending anything to anyone.
entries.summary: Lets the user test local microphone level before joining a huddle.
details: Opens the chosen microphone with the chosen processing through client-core's testMicrophone, the strong noise filter included, so what plays back is what a call would send; if the filter cannot start it says the browser's own suppression is standing in. It shows the microphone's name and level, and opens it again when the choice changes; autoStart listens at once, as the first-huddle question does. An optional playback sends the voice to the chosen speaker.
Nothing is sent to peers or the server. Stopping the check or closing settings stops the captured tracks.

entries.plain: The Voice & video settings, where you pick devices, set noise suppression and test your microphone, speaker and camera.
entries.summary: The Voice & video section of Account settings: devices, processing and tests.
details: Microphone, speaker (where setSinkId exists) and camera pickers with the system default first; a chosen device that is unplugged stays listed as such. Changes apply to a huddle in progress through chooseDevices and are kept for every workspace on this device.

Noise suppression as Strong, Standard or Off (Discord's choice; Strong unless chosen otherwise, and Off for anyone who had turned suppression off), echo cancellation and automatic volume switches, a microphone test with playback, a two-tone speaker test, a mirrored camera preview, and join-muted. When the browser keeps device names back it offers to ask for the microphone once.

entries.plain: Asks once, before your first huddle, which microphone and camera to use when you have more than one.
entries.summary: Asks once, before a first huddle, which microphone and camera to use.
details: callPreferences.joinHuddle asks when this device has not been asked (devicesChecked), nothing is chosen, and the browser lists more than one microphone or camera; a browser that keeps names back lists none, so it is asked on the first join after it gives them. Choosing a microphone or camera in settings counts as an answer.

The dialog, loaded on first use from WorkspaceScreen, listens through MicrophoneCheck and shows the camera through CameraPreview at once. Join huddle keeps the choice and joins with it; Cancel, or the workspace closing, joins nothing and asks again next time. Only a dialog that went without an answer calls the waiting join off.

entries.plain: Shows the full diagnostics report, call logs included, so you can read it before copying or saving it.
entries.summary: Shows the complete diagnostics report before copying or downloading it.
details: Reads server-info and optional owner/admin operating status, recording a readable failure when either is unavailable.
The person can inspect the report and choose copy or local text-file save; the dialog does not send diagnostics to another service.
The report includes this device's call log and, for the owner and admins, the server's call log, with people named by handle. Opened from a call that cannot connect, it starts at the call log.

entries.plain: A searchable list of keyboard shortcuts that follows your Enter to send setting.
entries.summary: Lists and filters keyboard shortcuts using the current composing preference.
details: Writing-key descriptions change with Enter-to-send so the help reflects active behavior.
A query matches words across keys and explanations, exposing navigation, message, formatting and call shortcuts without requiring the reader to memorize them.

entries.plain: Draws each person's colored initials and the dot that shows whether they are online.
entries.summary: Draws consistent initials avatars and presence indicators without image downloads.
details: Avatar uses the account's deterministic hue and display-name initials; missing users receive a fallback.
PresenceDot and AvatarWithPresence draw online state with a ring matching the parent surface, keeping the same visual rule across rows and calls.

entries.plain: The app's set of small icons and its logo, drawn directly so nothing extra has to download.
entries.summary: Provides the application's small inline SVG icon vocabulary and brand mark.
details: IconName maps to shared vector paths, stroke/size conventions and accessible usage supplied by parent controls.
Inline vectors avoid an icon font, extra network fetch and a large icon runtime dependency while keeping common controls visually consistent.

entries.plain: The app's standard buttons, in main, secondary, danger and quiet styles.
entries.summary: Centralizes primary, secondary, danger and quiet action styling.
details: buttonClass lets existing native buttons reuse variants; Button forwards native attributes and ref.
Preserves native button semantics, including form submission unless type=button is explicitly chosen.

entries.plain: The layer under every dialog, menu and full-size image, which keeps the keyboard inside the top one and returns focus on close.
entries.summary: Owns the shared stack of modal portals and keyboard/focus isolation.
details: Tracks the active layer, makes the page and older portals inert, and permits only the top layer to handle Escape, outside dismissal and tab containment.

Focus restoration follows connected usable openers and fallback owners even if an underlying dialog was removed. Layout registration accounts for child autoFocus occurring before portal ownership is fully installed.
Central ownership avoids competing independent focus traps for dialogs, menus and lightboxes.

entries.plain: The standard dialog frame with a title, a close button and matching form fields.
entries.summary: Adds standard dialog structure and form styling on top of Modal.
details: Supplies a titled surface, accessible description relationship, close affordance and configurable width.
Exports shared input classes so forms use the same focus, border and disabled appearance.

entries.plain: A small panel that opens beside the button that opened it, such as the choices for Send later.
entries.summary: A small panel anchored to the control that opened it, such as Send later's choices.
details: Built on the modal layer like Menu: Escape or a press outside closes it, the page beneath waits, and focus returns to the control. It sits above the control, or below when there is no room, and follows it as the page scrolls.

entries.plain: The compact menu used for message and workspace actions, which works by keyboard as well as by mouse.
entries.summary: Provides one accessible compact menu for row and workspace actions.
details: Built on the modal layer, with arrow navigation, Enter selection, Escape/outside dismissal and focus return to the trigger.
Repositions with scrolling instead of abandoning an action when a live timeline shifts. Destructive and disabled items keep consistent presentation.

entries.plain: The small hint that appears over a button when you point at it or reach it with the keyboard.
entries.summary: Explains compact controls without taking focus or blocking the page.
details: Hover opens after a short delay; keyboard focus opens immediately; Escape dismisses the hint. The floating portal follows its trigger and flips when needed.
Composes event handlers, accessible descriptions and refs, including React ref-cleanup behavior, so decorating a control does not replace its own lifetime contract.

entries.plain: Asks you to confirm before something that cannot be undone, and only goes ahead if you pick the named action.
entries.summary: Asks named questions for irreversible user actions and returns a boolean answer.
details: ConfirmProvider and useConfirm expose a promise resolved true only by the explicitly named action; cancellation, closing and Escape resolve false.
A destructive question begins on Cancel and can explain the consequence. Callers act on the answer rather than inferring permission from dismissal.

entries.plain: The small notices that say whether something worked, where failures stay until you dismiss them and may offer Retry or Undo.
entries.summary: Reports operation outcomes without interrupting current input.
details: Success notices clear after a reading interval, while failures remain for acknowledgement and can offer an operation-specific retry or undo.
A bounded stack pauses countdowns during hover/focus and preserves a nearby focus destination when a notice is removed. Notices never make the workspace inert.

entries.plain: Gives every list the same look while it is loading, refreshing, empty or offering to try again.
entries.summary: Keeps loading, refresh, empty and retry state consistent across lists.
details: Before first content it renders varied stand-in rows; later refreshes keep the current list and show a status line.

A stable live region and layout cleanup preserve focus when a Retry/empty-state action is replaced by results. This is a shared usability primitive rather than each panel inventing its own state layout.

entries.plain: Catches a part of the screen that breaks and offers to retry it, without losing your connection or what you typed.
entries.summary: Contains a broken React view while preserving the workspace connection and typed work.
details: Catches render failures and supplies recoverable fallback controls at the relevant boundary.
Dismissal can retry the same tree without automatically reloading the whole app, allowing the live client and unsent state outside that boundary to remain owned.

entries.plain: Shows a loading message while a panel or dialog downloads on first use, and offers to close or reload if that fails.
entries.summary: Wraps on-demand panels and dialogs with loading and failed-chunk recovery.
details: Suspense announces what is loading and retains a way to close the pending view.
An ErrorBoundary confines a failed download to that view and provides close/reload actions, allowing the rest of the workspace to remain usable.

flows.title: Sending a message
flows.summary: Different parts of Tandem look after what you type, the copy saved on your device and the message on the server. Sending passes the message along with a one-time code and waits for a confirmation, rather than just emptying the message box.

steps.title: Type and keep a draft
steps.description: The message box shows your words as you type them. The app saves the draft a moment after you pause, and right away when you switch conversations or close the app normally. A thread reply has its own draft, separate from the channel's.
steps.detail: Composer updates local text immediately, debounces client.setDraft for ordinary typing, and captures current text before navigation or normal close. Thread replies use their own draft key.

steps.title: Show the message right away
steps.description: The message shows up in the conversation right away, marked as sending, with previews of any attached files. The app gives it a random one-time code so it can recognise it later. If 50 messages are already waiting to send, the app refuses this one and keeps your draft.
steps.detail: WorkspaceClient validates admission, generates a random nonce, appends PendingMessage and creates local attachment previews. The 50-send limit refuses extra work while keeping the draft.

steps.title: Save it on the device before clearing the draft
steps.description: The message joins the messages waiting to send, saved on the device, and only then does the app clear the saved draft. The app counts the message as safe once it is saved on the device or delivered. If saving fails, the app keeps what it needs to try again or to give your words back.
steps.detail: DraftPersistence merges the outbox before clearing the corresponding saved draft. localWork settles the nonce after storage or delivery evidence; failures retain retry/recovery state.

steps.title: Upload files and post
steps.description: The app uploads any attached files, then sends the message to the server. If it has to try again, it does not upload the same files twice and sends exactly the same message. Upload progress shows on the message marked as sending.
steps.detail: deliver uploads chosen files, caches successful upload IDs for a retry and posts the exact message request. Progress belongs to the pending row.

steps.title: Swap in the confirmed message
steps.description: The server confirms the message, either in its answer or over the live connection. The app replaces the sending copy with the server's message, matched by its code, and frees the file previews. It removes the message from those waiting to send and leaves a note so an older copy cannot bring it back.
steps.detail: The HTTP response or WebSocket message.created event updates the replica and removes the optimistic entry by nonce. File previews are released and durable removal creates an outbox tombstone.

flows.detail: The visible draft, durable local work and server message each have different owners. Sending connects them with a nonce and acknowledgement rather than merely clearing the textarea.

flows.title: Picking up after a lost connection or restart
flows.summary: When something goes wrong, the app tells three cases apart. It may not know whether a message arrived, the server may have refused it, or an attached file may no longer be on the device, and in every case the same words must never quietly post twice.

steps.title: Show what went wrong
steps.description: A message that failed stays in the conversation, marked as sending, with the reason and what you can do. If the server refused it, it waits until you choose Retry. If the app cannot tell whether it arrived, it keeps the same code, so the server can spot a repeat.
steps.detail: A failed send stays in pending state with an actionable reason. A known refusal requires deliberate Retry; an uncertain outcome retains the same nonce.

steps.title: Note each change before saving it
steps.description: Before the app saves a change in the browser's storage, it first writes a quick note of the change. If the save fails or the page closes, the note stays and the change is made the next time the app starts. Each note records which tab made it and in what order, so a change already saved is never made twice.
steps.detail: deviceStore synchronously records the storage operation, then commits an IndexedDB transaction. Failure keeps the journal entry; tab/sequence metadata prevents repeating an operation already committed.

steps.title: Check the workspace before restoring
steps.description: The app restores saved work only after the server confirms which workspace and account this is, and the address is approved. It then reads the saved work for exactly that workspace and account. If the saved work cannot be read, the app offers to try again rather than starting empty.
steps.detail: The ready snapshot identifies workspace/account, WorkspaceStorageGate admits the address, and workspaceStorage reads the correct versioned keys. Unreadable storage offers retry instead of an empty alternate store.

steps.title: Restore unsent messages or their words
steps.description: The app restores messages saved as waiting to send and sends them again. Where the device kept only the words, they come back as text, unless that message was already sent or discarded. A message whose files are gone, or that is too old to resend on its own, waits for you to decide.
steps.detail: Durable outbox records restore sends; unstored recovery records restore words only when the outbox/tombstone does not own the nonce. Missing files and sends beyond the retry window remain held for the author.

steps.title: Catch up without a flood of notifications
steps.description: On reconnecting, the app tells the server the last update it saw and gets everything it missed, matched against the history it already has. Missed messages that still matter arrive as one catch-up summary instead of many notifications. A missed @here does not ring, since it was meant for people around at the time.
steps.detail: WebSocket hello sends lastSeq, replay is reconciled with snapshot-watermarked history, and eligible missed messages become a catch-up summary. @here replay is not treated as live presence.

flows.detail: Recovery distinguishes unknown network outcome, explicit server refusal and unavailable local attachment bytes. The same text must not silently become two sends.

flows.title: Using Tandem in two windows at once
flows.summary: When two windows save at once, Tandem merges each change in on its own, so neither window wipes out the other's drafts or deletions. The parts of the app that use these saves must still handle late answers themselves.

steps.title: Pick one place to save
steps.description: In a browser, the app keeps drafts and choices in one storage place and records that choice before moving older saved work into it. It does not switch places just because the browser cannot message other windows. If storage will not open, the app says it cannot be read and offers to try again.
steps.detail: N02 persists IndexedDB ownership before migration. Missing BroadcastChannel does not change ownership; failed opening remains unreadability with retry.

steps.title: Save only what changed
steps.description: Each save changes one thing in a single step, such as one conversation's draft, one message waiting to send, or one account's choice. If two windows typed different words into the same draft, the app keeps both. A message already sent or discarded cannot be brought back by an older copy.
steps.detail: A readwrite transaction merges one conversation's draft, one nonce's outbox state or one account's choice. Draft bases preserve conflicting words, and outbox tombstones/floors reject stale resurrection.

steps.title: Tell the other windows
steps.description: The app tells the other open windows what changed. If the usual route is missing, a backup signal names only what changed, and the other window reads it from storage. Windows also check again when you switch to them, and ignore late answers to older requests.
steps.detail: BroadcastChannel can deliver the change; a fallback storage event carries only the changed key, then reads IndexedDB. Focus refresh and generation guards supplement that path.

steps.title: Update the other window without losing its edits
steps.description: The other window takes in new drafts and messages waiting to send, without overwriting words you are still typing there. It also picks up a change to whether notifications show message previews. Edits you make there afterwards still merge correctly.
steps.detail: DraftPersistence adopts another window's drafts/outbox without overwriting its still-unsaved edits, while notification preview watchers update privacy choice. Newer local edits retain their own merge base.

steps.title: Three ways windows used to clash
steps.description: Three problems of this kind were repaired. Two windows opening a workspace at a new address at the same moment can no longer both trust it. A late reply can no longer undo a newer choice about notification previews. A window left open can no longer bring back a saved sign-in another window removed, or erase one it added.
steps.detail: Q02 made first-address registration atomic, Q03 fences old preference replies against newer watches, and Q05 makes each saved sign-in change a turn against the stored list.

flows.detail: Atomic backend merges preserve changed keys and removals. Caller-level state still needs its own reply-order ownership; Q02, Q03 and Q05 closed three such gaps.

flows.title: Joining a huddle
flows.summary: Joining a huddle means loading your call settings, getting your microphone, being let in by the server and connecting to everyone else. If your microphone changes during the call, your latest mute choice carries over.

steps.title: Load your call settings
steps.description: The huddle button in the channel header and the one in Getting started both wait until your call settings have loaded or finished saving. If the settings cannot be read, you join with the microphone off and can try loading them again. Moving elsewhere first can cancel a join you no longer want.
steps.detail: Header and Getting started actions wait for current initialization or saving. Unreadable preferences keep the microphone off and expose retry; a navigation guard can cancel a join no longer wanted.

steps.title: Get the microphone first
steps.description: The app reads the server's call connection settings and sets up the call. It asks for your microphone and applies your current mute choice to it. If you cancelled and the microphone arrives late, the app turns it off at once.
steps.detail: WorkspaceClient reads RTC configuration and creates HuddleSession. startLocalAudio requests the microphone and adopts it with the current mute intent; late media after cancellation is stopped.

steps.title: Join and connect to others
steps.description: The server confirms the join, and if joining fails, the app lets go of the microphone. For each pair of people, one side starts the connection. Fixed slots carry the microphone, camera and screen share.
steps.detail: Supported servers acknowledge huddle.join with a request ID; failure cleans local media. The roster chooses one offerer per peer and fixed microphone/camera/screen transceivers carry streams.

steps.title: Play each voice once
steps.description: Each person's voice plays once, at the volume you chose for them, while video tiles stay silent. The small huddle bar shows who is speaking. The larger call view loads only when you open it and fits cameras and screen shares to the space.
steps.detail: HuddleAudio owns remote voices, each as loud as you chose; video tiles stay muted. Speaking transitions update the compact bar, while the lazy stage fits cameras and shares to the available container.

steps.title: Switch microphones or leave
steps.description: If your microphone disconnects, the app picks up the new default one, applies your current mute choice and passes it to everyone in the call. Leaving turns off your microphone and camera, stops watching for device changes and closes every connection.
steps.detail: After microphone loss, recovery captures the new default, applies the current mute choice and replaceTrack updates peers. Leave/destroy stops tracks, polling, device listeners and peer connections.

flows.detail: A join has owned preference initialization, permission capture, server admission and peer media. The latest mute choice follows a replacement microphone.

flows.title: Filling in a form from an app
flows.summary: Each form an app opens keeps its own answers and its own result, so a late reply to an old form cannot close a new one. The server also refuses a second submission of the same form while one is in progress, but after an unclear network failure the app itself may need to spot a repeat.

steps.title: Receive the form
steps.description: The server tells only you that an app added to the workspace wants to show you a form. The app engine adds it to the workspace, and the screens open it in a dialog tied to that form's own ID.
steps.detail: A server ephemeral opens a ModalView in the workspace replica. ViewModal renders an AppForm keyed by that unique view ID.

steps.title: Fill in the fields
steps.description: Each field keeps its own answer. Whether the form is busy, its errors and its messages all belong to this one form. Nothing is saved on the device.
steps.detail: Each block/action pair has its own value key. Busy, errors and message state belong to this keyed instance; nothing is saved to device storage.

steps.title: Submit once
steps.description: Pressing submit again while the first is under way does nothing. The app engine checks it is still the same form, then sends your answers to the server.
steps.detail: An immediate submitting guard blocks a second local submit. WorkspaceClient checks the captured view ID, and Api submits the nested answer payload to the server.

steps.title: Accept only this form's result
steps.description: If the app accepts the answers, this form closes. If it refuses a field, that field gets the focus. If the network fails, you see a message, but only while this form is still open.
steps.detail: Success dismisses the original view ID, validation focuses its refused field, and a transport failure reports a message only while this instance remains alive.

steps.title: Start a new form fresh
steps.description: When the app sends a new form, the old one disappears and the new one starts empty. A late result from the old form cannot close or change the new one. The server separately refuses a second submission of a form that is still being handled.
steps.detail: A new view ID unmounts the old form and starts fresh state. N05 prevents the prior callback result from closing or contaminating it; N08 provides separate server-side in-flight exclusion.

flows.detail: A form's identity owns its input and completion. The server additionally excludes concurrent submissions of that same view, while external uncertain retries can still require app-side deduplication.

flows.title: Following a link to a workspace or message
flows.summary: Opening a link answers four separate questions, each in its own place. The link says where to go, a saved sign-in says who you are, the trusted address decides whether work saved on the device may open, and history remembers where to return.

steps.title: Read the link
steps.description: The desktop app or the browser hands over a Tandem link it recognises. Tandem then picks a saved sign-in, reuses the workspace already open, or keeps the target message in mind while you join.
steps.detail: Platform consumes a recognized desktop or browser fragment link. App chooses a remembered sign-in, reuses the open workspace or carries a message target through joining.

steps.title: Sign in and identify the workspace
steps.description: The join screen checks that the server works with this version of Tandem and signs you in, then the app engine receives the workspace. Switching workspaces fully shuts down the previous one, so no old connection or call keeps running behind the new screen.
steps.detail: JoinScreen probes compatibility and authenticates, then WorkspaceClient receives the ready snapshot. Switching destroys the previous client so no old socket/media remains active behind the new screen.

steps.title: Approve the address before opening saved work
steps.description: Before opening drafts and other work saved on the device, the app checks that this exact address is approved for this workspace and account. A different address for the same workspace needs your approval. Two windows registering a first address at the same moment are settled in one step, so only one is trusted without asking.
steps.detail: WorkspaceStorageGate checks the exact connected address for the authenticated workspace/account before mounting local-work consumers. Later aliases require approval; simultaneous first registration is settled atomically (Q02).

steps.title: Jump to the message
steps.description: The app opens the right channel, thread or panel and loads the part of the history around the message. It highlights the message, and stops the usual loading of older messages from pulling the view away while it scrolls there.
steps.detail: WorkspaceScreen chooses the channel/thread/panel and requests an owned jump window. The timeline highlights the message while keeping ordinary paging from fighting the programmatic scroll.

steps.title: Make Back and Forward work
steps.description: Back and Forward return to places in this workspace and to where you were reading, including in threads during this session. Closing a panel or dialog returns the keyboard to the button that opened it.
steps.detail: route.ts records workspace-bound places and reading anchors, threadPosition bounds session thread anchors, and panel/modal focus helpers return keyboard focus to a usable opener. Q06 and Q11 closed the abandoned-action navigation paths.

flows.detail: Link parsing, account restoration, address trust and history each answer a different question: destination, credentials, local-work admission and reading position.
